newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish central bank caps bullish zloty at parity.
newsitem.headline: Polish central bank caps bullish zloty at parity.

text.p: The zloty jumped to its highest level in a month on Monday and had to be capped by currency-buying intervention after the central bank signalled it may tighten Poland's monetary screws.

In a Saturday newspaper a senior NBP official said the bank may again tighten monetary policy because commercial banks were not sufficiently raising credit and deposit rates after last week's official interest rate increase.
Dealers said that foreign investors remained on the sidelines on Monday and that the zloty soared against the basket as domestic banks reduced foreign currency positions.
"There were no foreigners and domestic speculation and position adjustments gave the zloty a boost," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Some said large foreign capital inflows into the Warsaw bourse, which rose 5.2 percent on Friday and 3.3 percent on Monday, may have also boosted the zloty.

The zloty briefly climbed above the parity rate, the first time the local unit crossed the mid-point of its trading band since its mid-July decline amid mounting worries over flood losses, a gaping external deficit and parliamentary elections.

It closed at minus 0.26/0.31 percent from the trading band centre, against Friday's close at minus 0.73/0.88 percent after the central bank bought at least $20 million when the zloty was hovering slightly above the parity rate.
The zloty was at 3.4685/00 to the dollar, against 3.4850/00 on Friday and at 1.8690/00 to the mark, against 1.8750/80.
Dealers said, however, that despite recent gains the zloty would probably remain locked in a range between parity and minus 1.5 percent ahead of parliamentary polls on September 21.

"The NBP may have stabilised the market by intervening because now the zloty resistance is at parity and the bank earlier gave the local unit support around minus 1.5 percent," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.

Dealers said the market's pro-zloty sentiment would likely run out of steam because longer-term foreign investors would likely stay clear of Polish treasuries ahead of elections and only speculators would dabble in the zloty in the coming month.
"This strengthening could be a short-term shot in the arm but the (up) trend could still be reversed ahead of elections," said Miroslaw Winiarczyk, forex dealer at BDK SA.

The NBP said in the Saturday paper its further monetary policy tightening would also depend on how the state-owned PKO BP - the country's biggest savings bank -- would react to the central bank's recent rate rise.

"We are still waiting for the reaction of (the state savings bank) PKO BP, but basically we already know that the hitherto (rate) increases in commercial banks are too small," NBP monetary policy head Jerzy Stopyra was quoted as saying.
"We may use other (monetary policy) instruments," he said.
On August 4 the NBP increased its lombard rate by two points to 27 percent and discount by 2.5 to 24.5 percent.
The management board of PKO BP is due to meet on Tuesday to decide the bank's new rate levels after PKO sigalled that it would increase rates last week.
